text: {"domains":{"block_M":[64,128],"block_N":[64,128,256],"block_K":[32,64],"num_stages":[1,2,3,4],"threads":[64,128],"swizzle":[0,4,8,16,32,64]},"shared_memory_limit":32768,"weights":{"traffic":1,"launches":1,"pipeline":1.5,"footprint":0.5},"rationale":"Attempt-04 (64x128x32,s2,t128,sw64) improved best simulated latency to 462.42us vs 470.76us, confirming deeper pipelining (stages=2) helps more than swizzle, which has been latency-neutral with invariant 16.78MB DRAM across all runs; the analytic panel-reuse hypothesis remains unsupported, so I upweight pipeline (1.5) and downweight footprint (0.5) to steer HiGHS toward deeper K pipelines within the 32768 cap, while keeping traffic=1 since DRAM did not vary. Retain block_M=[64,128] (block_M=32 corner regressed twice), block_N=[64,128,256], block_K=[32,64], full swizzle, and stages up to 4 to probe pipeline depth. Changed thread domain to [64,128]: single 128 domain risked stagnation, 256 correlated with the worst run, so add 64 to test warp layout while staying on the fast side. Next hypothesis: block_M=128 with stages=3-4 and threads=64/128 reduces latency below 462.42us; also test block_N=128 vs 256 at deeper stages. Scope: Metal executes exact source/config/TIR; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed."}
